ledger.note: 1885 (27 February): the German East Africa Company receives its imperial charter. 'Established by the DOAG: 27 February 1885'; the charter was 'signed by Chancellor Otto von Bismarck on 27 February 1885'; capital Bagamoyo (1885-1890).

region.text: the coastal strip round Bagamoyo, the Abushiri revolt

ledger.note: 1888: the coast rises against the Company. 'The Abushiri Revolt of 1888 was put down with British help the following year', a revolt against 'the activities of the German East Africa Company'. The page gives no boundary for the revolt; the coast opposite Zanzibar is the researcher's reading.

region.text: German East Africa's mainland, the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty sphere

ledger.note: 1890 (1 July): the Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty fixes the German sphere. 'Heligoland-Zanzibar Treaty: 1 July 1890' 'decided the border between GEA and the East Africa Protectorate', 'unsurveyed until 1910'. The page does not say the mainland became a colony by this treaty; the Imperial administration (High Commissioners from 1888 or 1891) took over from the Company.

region.text: the Kionga triangle on the Rovuma, 'virtually forced Portugal to cede the triangle in 1894'

ledger.note: 1894: Germany takes the Kionga triangle. 'Germany had virtually forced Portugal to cede the triangle in 1894.'
1897: Germany reaches Rwanda. 'In 1897, the German Empire established a presence in Rwanda with the formation of an alliance with the king.'

1897: Burundi joins Rwanda as a German district. The Ruanda-Urundi page says only that Ruanda and Urundi 'were administered as two districts of German East Africa' and dates nothing for Burundi; the year bridges with Rwanda's.

region.text: the colony, fought over by Britain, Belgium and Portugal

ledger.note: 1914 (3 August): the East African campaign begins. 'East African campaign: 3 August 1914'; 'on 8 August HMS Astraea shelled the wireless station at Dar es Salaam'.

1916 (May): Belgian forces occupy Ruanda. 'Ruanda was occupied over April-May and Urundi in June 1916'; infobox 'Belgian occupation: 6 May 1916'; the East African campaign page has the Force Publique capturing Kigali on 6 May.

1916 (June): Belgian forces occupy Urundi ('Urundi in June 1916'). 'By September, a large portion of German East Africa was under Belgian occupation reaching as far south as Kigoma and Karema and as far eastwards as Tabora'; Smuts later ordered the Belgians back, leaving them in Rwanda and Burundi.

region.text: Kigoma and Ujiji, the western end of the Central Railway

ledger.note: 1916 (September): the British hold the Central Railway, here its western end at Kigoma and Ujiji. 'the railway from Dar es Salaam to Ujiji' was 'fully under British control' by September 1916; the capital moves to Tabora temporarily (infobox 'Tabora (1916, temporary)'), where 'the Germans were defeated and the village occupied' on 19 September. The Dar es Salaam capture date is not on the page. ledger.note: 1919 (28 June): the colony is formally dissolved. Infobox 'Formal disestablishment: 28 June 1919'; 'The Treaty of Versailles was signed on 28 June 1919, although the treaty did not take effect until 10 January 1920'; the territory was 'divided amongst Britain, Belgium and Portugal'. Tanganyika became the British territory's name on 10 January 1920, and the Commission on Mandates agreed on 12 July 1919 to give the Kionga triangle to Portugal.

wars.name: East African campaign (World War I)
wars.outcome: Allied victory: Belgians in Ruanda and Urundi in 1916, the British on the Central Railway by September 1916, Lettow-Vorbeck into Mozambique on 23 November 1917 and surrender at Abercorn on 25 November 1918; the colony divided among Britain, Belgium and Portugal in 1919.
wars.note: The page has Britain declaring war on 4 August 1914; the infobox gives 3 August 1914 to 25 November 1918.

notes:
Cliopatria has no German East Africa row (its German Africa aggregate runs 1871-1918). Every keyframe is new. The colony's core in 1885 is the researcher's circle round Bagamoyo: the page gives treaties without boundaries.
Not settled: how the Imperial administration replaced the Company (the page lists High Commissioners from 1888 and Governors from 1891, no date for the takeover); the 1890 'gain' is the treaty's recognition of the sphere, at confidence 2; the Burundi year (page silent, confidence 1); the Anglo-German boundary of 1910 survey and the Kivu-Mfumbiro dispute with Belgium and Britain over the Rwanda frontier (not on the page); the Maji Maji dates; the Dar es Salaam capture date. The Treaty of Versailles took effect on 10 January 1920, so Tanganyika, Ruanda-Urundi and Kionga were administered by the Allies from 1916 to the mandates.
Counterparts needing dossiers: tanganyika-territory (1919-1961, the British mandate and trust; I intend one if budget allows), ruanda-urundi (1916-1962, this batch), Abushiri and Maji Maji (rebel movements, not states). Gazetteer: 'Kionga Triangle' (region) is a real name the gazetteer lacks; 'Tanganyika' (region) is used for the Maji Maji zone and may also be missing.
